chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The flu is an army from the armies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends it to the illness to eradicate it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic view on the cause and purpose of the flu according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) conveys that the Prophet (saww) identified nasal congestion (zukaam) as a 'soldier' of Allah, illustrating the Shia concept of 'amrad' (illness) as a purposeful, active agent rather than a passive defect. This view aligns with the theological principle that bodily ailments serve as divine mechanisms to expel internal impurities or diseases, reflecting a holistic understanding of health where suffering has a specific, curative function.
